title: What New York clubs pay and an exploitative Sunday offer
summary: Clubs pay little or nothing; she turned down a job running Sunday shows for a percentage of the door; New Jersey and Connecticut pay somewhat better.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do the clubs in New York generally have a standard rate that they would pay for a group?
You mean a standard rate of zero.
A standard rate of zero or do they make you pay? I mean I’ve heard clubs, or maybe not in jazz but I know there’s some clubs where the bands actually have to pay.

It’s true. I mean there’s so many great jazz musicians. They come from all over the world and then the students graduating from the colleges, and the clubs really do know that they have a free meal. So they tend not to pay union scale. There may be one that does, I don’t know. And some will just pay you what they get at the door or a percent of that. I recently had a club ask me to run the Sunday afternoon shows and hire the band and be the guest artist and, you know, that’s a fairly heavy responsibility. And when I asked about what my fee would be or how much could I pay the bands, that was my first question. They said, “Well whatever comes in at the door we give 70% of the door.” So that put me in a position of being one of them. You know I’m supposed to call bands and then ask them to play and give them this great opportunity and then say, but you only get —
You don’t even know what you’re going to get.

That’s right. And then I ask what my fee would be for doing this and he said, “Oh well we’ll give you a percent of their percent.” So that made it even more exploitative. And so you know I had to say no even though I would have loved to have that job on Sundays. I mean it’s a good opportunity for me to play as well with whoever you want to hire. But how can you do it without money? I mean you can go only so far without money and then it becomes too much. So the clubs pay fairly low and some of them will allow you to get © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

tips and others won’t, they won’t hear of it. And so it’s rough that way. And then when you get a little bit outside New York like New Jersey or Connecticut you already find a difference there where you get a little bit more. And so a lot of people do that. There’s the Shanghai Club in New Jersey or there’s a lot of clubs in Connecticut, upstate New York.
Yes. And there’s the universities and so forth.
Yeah. That’s a whole different story.
